06-01.t: First Classes Begin at Calcutta Medical College
06-01.s: Academic classes commenced at Medical College & Hospital, Kolkata (Calcutta Medical College), marking the formal beginning of modern Western medical education in eastern India.
French neurologist and psychiatrist Jules Cotard, who described Cotard's syndrome (Cotard delusion) in 1882, was born.
At the Société de Biologie in Paris, Charles-Édouard Brown-Séquard reported self-injecting an extract of animal testis, sparking early organotherapy and endocrinology research.

06-01.t: Data Collection Begins for National Mental Health Survey of India
06-01.s: Field data collection began for the landmark National Mental Health Survey of India (2015-16) coordinated by NIMHANS, providing India's first comprehensive nationwide epidemiological baseline of mental disorders.

06-02.s: British physician Sir Samuel Wilks, a founding figure of clinical science who helped describe ulcerative colitis and myasthenia gravis, was born in London.
Japanese-American chemist Jokichi Takamine was granted the first patent for adrenaline (epinephrine), enabling its standardized clinical use.

06-02.t: All-India Institute of Medical Sciences Act, 1956 Commences
06-02.s: The All-India Institute of Medical Sciences Act, 1956 (Act 25 of 1956) was published and commenced, establishing AIIMS New Delhi as an autonomous institution of national importance for medical education, research, and tertiary care.

06-02.t: Passing of Obstetrician-Gynecologist Dr. Jerusha Jhirad
06-02.s: Padma Shri physician Dr. Jerusha Jacob Jhirad passed away at age 93. She was the first Indian superintendent of Cama Hospital in Mumbai and conducted landmark statistical inquiries into maternal mortality.

06-03.s: English physician William Harvey, who discovered the systemic circulation of blood pumped by the heart, died at age 79.

06-03.t: First Published Account of Subcutaneous Opiate Injection
06-03.s: Irish surgeon Francis Rynd at Meath Hospital treated severe facial neuralgia by introducing a morphine-creosote solution subcutaneously, marking the first published account of hypodermic opiate injection.

06-04.s: American dermatologist John Addison Fordyce, who described Fordyce spots and Fox-Fordyce disease, was born.

06-04.t: James Ramsay Hunt Describes Ramsay Hunt Syndrome
06-04.s: American neurologist James Ramsay Hunt presented his description of herpes zoster oticus involving the geniculate ganglion and causing ipsilateral facial palsy to the American Neurological Association.

06-04.t: Birth of Bio-organic Chemist Dr. Darshan Ranganathan
06-04.s: Renowned Indian bio-organic chemist Dr. Darshan Ranganathan was born in Delhi; she later pioneered work in protein folding, self-assembling peptide nanotubes, and chemical simulation of the urea cycle.

Dr. Darshan Ranganathan passed away on her 60th birthday following a battle with breast cancer, leaving a prolific legacy in peptide chemistry and inspiring the biennial Professor Darshan Ranganathan Memorial Lecture.

06-05.s: In his first Harben Lecture in London, Paul Ehrlich outlined targeted therapy, likening antitoxins and antimicrobials to "charmed bullets" (Zauberkugeln) that selectively destroy pathogens.

06-05.t: CDC Publishes First Official Report of AIDS
06-05.s: The U.S. CDC's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report published a report of five cases of Pneumocystis carinii pneumonia in previously healthy young men in Los Angeles, marking the first official report of AIDS.

06-06.s: German-born Austrian physiologist Ernst Wilhelm von Brücke, who described the Brücke reflex and the red reflex of the eye (1845-1847), was born.
American cardiologist Paul Dudley White, a co-describer of Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome (1930) and the McGinn-White pattern (1935), was born.

06-07.s: American obstetrical anesthesiologist Virginia Apgar, inventor of the 10-point Apgar score to rapidly evaluate newborn health and reduce infant mortality, was born.

06-07.t: Constitution of the Indian Red Cross Society
06-07.s: Fifty members were formally nominated to constitute the Indian Red Cross Society under the Indian Red Cross Society Act (Act XV of 1920), establishing India's national humanitarian and disaster-relief health organization.
American cardiologist Bernard Lown, developer of the direct-current (DC) defibrillator and cardioverter and co-describer of Lown-Ganong-Levine syndrome, was born.

06-08.s: German medical illustrator Max Brödel, who introduced the carbon dust technique for half-tone anatomical realism and described Brödel's suture, was born.

06-08.t: CDC Establishes Task Force on Kaposi's Sarcoma and Opportunistic Infections
06-08.s: The U.S. CDC established a task force to investigate clusters of Pneumocystis carinii pneumonia and Kaposi's sarcoma, forming the first national surveillance framework for the emerging AIDS epidemic.

06-09.s: English physiologist and pharmacologist Sir Henry Dale was born in London. He shared the 1936 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for establishing acetylcholine as a chemical neurotransmitter.
French veterinarian, bacteriologist, and immunologist Camille Guérin, who co-developed the Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine against tuberculosis with Albert Calmette, died.

06-10.s: Akron surgeon Dr. Bob Smith took his last alcoholic drink after meeting Bill Wilson, marking the official founding date of Alcoholics Anonymous.

06-10.t: First Successful Intracardiac Operation for Mitral Stenosis
06-10.s: Surgeon Charles Philamore Bailey in Philadelphia performed the first anatomically conceived, digitally guided intracardiac operation on a 24-year-old woman with severe mitral stenosis.

06-11.s: Australian pathologist J. Robin Warren, who won the 2005 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for co-discovering Helicobacter pylori, was born in Adelaide.
American endocrinologist Jerome W. Conn, who described primary hyperaldosteronism (Conn's syndrome) in 1955 and helped define the renin-aldosterone axis, died.

06-11.t: National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) Formed
06-11.s: The National Commission for Indian System of Medicine officially came into existence, replacing the Central Council of Indian Medicine to regulate education and practice in Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani, and Sowa-Rigpa.

06-12.s: English neurologist Charles Edward Beevor, known for describing Beevor's sign and Beevor's axiom on brain motor control, was born.
French neurologist Théophile Alajouanine, who co-described Foix-Alajouanine syndrome and Marie-Foix-Alajouanine syndrome, was born.

06-13.s: The University of Sydney formally established Australia's first Faculty of Medicine when its Senate appointed a Board of Examiners.
American gastroenterologist Burrill Bernard Crohn, who described regional ileitis (Crohn's disease) in 1932, was born.

06-13.t: Passing of Sir Ram Nath Chopra, Father of Indian Pharmacology
06-13.s: Colonel Sir Ram Nath Chopra passed away in Srinagar at age 90. Celebrated as the Father of Indian Pharmacology, he chaired the 1930-31 Drugs Enquiry Committee and pioneered research on indigenous medicinal plants such as Rauvolfia serpentina.

06-14.t: First Smallpox Vaccination Administered in India
06-14.s: Three-year-old Anna Dusthall in Bombay (Mumbai) became the first person in India to receive the smallpox vaccine, initiating a chain of human-to-human lymph vaccination that spread to Madras, Poona, Hyderabad, and Surat.
Austrian-American immunologist Karl Landsteiner, who identified the ABO blood group system in 1901 and won the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, was born.
Urologist Frederic Eugene Basil Foley first publicly exhibited his self-retaining balloon catheter at the American Medical Association meeting in Atlantic City.

06-15.s: French physician Jean-Baptiste Denys administered the first fully documented human blood transfusion, infusing sheep blood into a 15-year-old boy who survived.

06-16.s: English physician John Snow, a founder of modern epidemiology and pioneer of anesthesia, medical hygiene, and public health, died.
American physician Crawford Williamson Long, credited with the first surgical use of inhaled sulphuric ether for anesthesia, died.

06-17.s: French physician and surgeon Auguste Nélaton, who described Nélaton's line and invented the Nélaton probe in 1862, was born.
Surgeon Richard H. Lawler led the team at Little Company of Mary Hospital in Evergreen Park, Illinois, performing the world's first successful human kidney transplant on Ruth Tucker.

06-18.s: French physician Charles Louis Alphonse Laveran was born in Paris. He discovered the malaria parasite and won the 1907 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his work on pathogenic protozoa.

06-18.t: FDA Panel Unanimously Backs Moderna mRNA Flu Vaccine
06-18.s: The FDA's Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee voted 9-0 to recommend Moderna's mRNA-based influenza vaccine for adults aged 50 and older.

06-19.s: Italian-born American surgeon and anesthetist Angelo Luigi Soresi, who defined the hanging-drop technique for epidural anesthesia and early diaphragmatic hernia repair, was born.
Uruguayan pediatrician Luís Morquio, who described Morquio syndrome (mucopolysaccharidosis type IV) in 1929, died.

06-19.t: Passing of IVF Pioneer Dr. Subhash Mukhopadhyay
06-19.s: Physician and physiologist Dr. Subhash Mukhopadhyay passed away in Kolkata. In 1978, he had created India's first and the world's second test-tube baby, Kanupriya Agarwal (Durga), using cryopreserved embryos, an achievement formally recognized years after his death.

06-20.s: English biochemist Sir Frederick Gowland Hopkins was born in Eastbourne, England. He shared the 1929 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering essential growth-stimulating vitamins.

06-20.t: Birth of India's First Female Cardiologist Dr. S. I. Padmavati
06-20.s: Padma Vibhushan awardee Dr. Sivaramakrishna Iyer Padmavati was born in 1917. She established India's first cardiac clinic and cardiac catheterization laboratory and founded the All India Heart Foundation.

06-21.t: First Medical Diploma in America Granted
06-21.s: The College of Philadelphia granted the first medical diploma in America to Dr. John Archer.

06-21.t: Lou Gehrig Retires Following ALS Diagnosis
06-21.s: The New York Yankees announced Lou Gehrig's retirement after physicians revealed he had amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), bringing widespread public attention to the neurodegenerative disease.

06-21.t: Universal Free COVID-19 Vaccination Drive Begins with Record 8.6M Doses
06-21.s: India commenced its universalized free COVID-19 vaccination drive for all adults, administering a then-record 8.6 million doses on the opening day.

06-22.s: Scottish surgeon Sir William Macewen, a pioneer of modern neurosurgery who described Macewen's sign and Macewen's osteotomy, was born.

06-22.t: First Successful Reversal of Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
06-22.s: Claude Schaeffer Beck, Edward C. Weckesser, and Frederick M. Barry achieved the first successful reversal of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, demonstrating that defibrillation could restore life after sudden cardiac death.

06-23.s: French pediatrician Antoine Bernard-Jean Marfan, who described Marfan syndrome in 1896, was born.
English surgeon, dermatologist, and ophthalmologist Sir Jonathan Hutchinson, who described Hutchinson's teeth and Hutchinson's triad of congenital syphilis, died.

06-23.t: India Surpasses 300 Million COVID-19 Vaccine Doses
06-23.s: India crossed the milestone of 300 million cumulative COVID-19 vaccine doses administered nationwide.

06-24.s: German anatomist and physiologist Ernst Heinrich Weber, who described the Weber tuning-fork test (1834) and Weber's law, was born.
German bacteriologist Friedrich Loeffler, known for co-discovering the bacterium causing diphtheria and identifying the foot-and-mouth disease virus, was born.

06-24.t: Passing of Dr. Ramchandra Dattatraya Lele, Father of Nuclear Medicine in India
06-24.s: Padma Bhushan physician Dr. Ramchandra Dattatraya Lele passed away. Widely regarded as the Father of Nuclear Medicine in India, he pioneered clinical nuclear imaging and radioisotope therapeutics in the country.

06-25.t: Eduard Jaeger Ritter von Jaxtthal Born
06-25.s: Austrian ophthalmologist Eduard Jaeger von Jaxtthal, who provided the first description of diabetic retinopathy (1855) and developed Jaeger reading test-types, was born.
English physiologist Henry Cuthbert Bazett, who formulated Bazett's formula (1920) for correcting the QT interval for heart rate, was born.

06-26.s: Scottish surgeon James Syme, known for describing the Syme ankle disarticulation amputation in 1831, died.
Austrian-American immunologist Karl Landsteiner, who identified the ABO blood group system in 1901 and transformed transfusion medicine, died.

06-27.s: French physician Armand Trousseau, who described Trousseau's sign of latent tetany (1861) and Trousseau's syndrome of malignancy-associated thrombosis, died.
American endocrinologist Grant Winder Liddle, who described Liddle syndrome (1963) and introduced the dexamethasone suppression test (1960), was born.

06-28.s: French physician Pierre Paul Broca, who identified the brain's speech production region (Broca's area) and described Broca's aphasia, was born.
English pediatrician Sir George Frederic Still, who described systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (Still's disease) in 1896 and Still's murmur in 1909, died.

06-29.s: English physician Thomas Addison, who first described primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease) and Addison-Biermer pernicious anemia, died at age 67.
American surgeon William James Mayo, co-founder of the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota, was born in Le Sueur, Minnesota.

06-30.s: French physician Auguste Louis Jules Millard, who described Millard-Gubler brainstem syndrome in 1856, was born.
American surgeon and urologist Gordon David Oppenheimer, one of the three authors of the foundational 1932 description of regional ileitis (later named Crohn's disease), was born.

06-30.t: Founding of Kasturba Medical College (KMC), Manipal
06-30.s: Dr. T. M. A. Pai established Kasturba Medical College in Manipal as India's first private, self-financing MBBS medical college, later expanding into Manipal Academy of Higher Education.
